chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn Wahb asked Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام about the best thing by which the servants draw near to their Lord, and which of that is most beloved to Allah, Mighty and Majestic. So he said:
"I do not know of anything after maʿrifah that is better than this salat (prayer). Do you not see that the righteous servant, ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام, said:
"And He has enjoined upon me salat (prayer)."

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer), the foremost act of worship after maʿrifah
key_terms.الْعَبْدَ الصَّالِحَ: the righteous servant, referring here to ʿĪsā عليه السلام
key_terms.الْمَعْرِفَةِ: recognition and knowledge of Allah in context
key_terms.رَبِّهِمْ: their Lord, to Whom nearness is sought
key_terms.عِيسَى ابْنَ مَرْيَمَ: Jesus son of Mary عليه السلام

ai.seo_question: What is the best act after maʿrifah for drawing near to Allah according to Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that after maʿrifah, salat (prayer) is the greatest means by which the servants draw near to Allah عَزَّ وَجَلَّ. The Imam عليه السلام reinforces this by citing the words of ʿĪsā ibn Maryam عليه السلام, showing the centrality of prayer in divine religion.
